newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel sharply higher against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel sharply higher against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose sharply against the dollar on Thursday in quiet trading, dealers said.

"The market continues to be very quiet and activity is low. The market is stabilising and the spreads in interbank trading are now at 50-70 points (against 100-150 earlier this week)," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.
"The session opened with higher supply of foreign currency but just towards the setting of the representative rate investors started converting shekels," he said.
The dealer added that companies are still waiting to see where the market is going. "The business sector is sitting on the fence waiting for further information," he said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5520 shekels against 3.5690 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.8551 against 3.8701 on Wednesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 3.1471 shekels per 100 yen compared with 3.1663 on Wednesday, and against the mark at 2.0235 shekels compared with 2.0254 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5530 shekels.
-- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
